symptom: PC in VLAN 20 cannot reach another host in VLAN 20.
topology_note: SW1 connects PC-A and PC-B; both should be access ports in VLAN 20.
show_outputs:
SW1#show vlan brief
10  SALES active Fa0/1, Fa0/2
20  STAFF active Fa0/3
SW1#show interfaces Fa0/4 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
expected_fault: Fa0/4 is in VLAN 1 instead of required VLAN 20.
expected_fix: Configure Fa0/4 as access VLAN 20, then verify with show vlan brief.

symptom: Users on SW2 lose access to VLAN 30 servers after a trunk is configured.
topology_note: SW1-SW2 is an 802.1Q trunk; VLANs 10,20,30 must cross it.
show_outputs:
SW2#show interfaces trunk
Port Fa0/1 Status trunking
Port Fa0/1 Vlans allowed on trunk 10,20
SW2#show vlan brief
30 SERVERS active
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is not allowed on the SW1-SW2 trunk.
expected_fix: Allow VLAN 30 on the trunk and verify trunk VLAN list.

symptom: A phone/PC access port reports no connectivity after moving the PC to VLAN 40.
topology_note: SW1 Fa0/8 should serve an IP phone/PC data VLAN 40.
show_outputs:
SW1#show vlan brief
40 VOICE active Fa0/9
SW1#show interfaces Fa0/8 switchport
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
expected_fault: Fa0/8 is still assigned to VLAN 1 rather than VLAN 40.
expected_fix: Set the access VLAN to 40 and verify host connectivity.

symptom: Two PCs on the same switch cannot communicate even though IP addresses are in the same subnet.
topology_note: PC-A is on Fa0/5 and PC-B on Fa0/6; both should be VLAN 50.
show_outputs:
SW1#show vlan brief
50 ENGINEERING active Fa0/5
60 TEST active Fa0/6
PC-A 192.168.50.10/24
PC-B 192.168.50.11/24
expected_fault: The two switch ports are in different VLANs (50 and 60).
expected_fix: Place both ports in the intended VLAN 50, after human review.

symptom: PC gets an IP but cannot reach a remote subnet.
topology_note: PC-A is in 192.168.10.0/24; R1 G0/0 is the gateway.
show_outputs:
PC-A: IP 192.168.10.25 Mask 255.255.255.0 Gateway 192.168.10.254
R1#show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.10.1 up up
expected_fault: PC-A uses gateway 192.168.10.254, but the router interface is 192.168.10.1.
expected_fix: Correct the PC gateway to 192.168.10.1 (or intentionally configure a matching gateway after review).

symptom: Host can ping same-subnet devices but not the internet.
topology_note: LAN 192.168.20.0/24 connects to R1 G0/0.
show_outputs:
PC-A: IP 192.168.20.15 Mask 255.255.255.0 Gateway 192.168.30.1
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/0 192.168.20.1 up up
expected_fault: Host default gateway is on a different subnet (192.168.30.1).
expected_fix: Set the host gateway to 192.168.20.1 and retest.

symptom: Only one subnet has remote connectivity failure while local pings work.
topology_note: VLAN 70 clients use R1 as their default gateway.
show_outputs:
PC-A: IP 10.70.0.20 Mask 255.255.255.0 Gateway 10.70.0.254
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/1 10.70.0.1 up up
expected_fault: The client gateway does not match the active R1 interface for VLAN 70.
expected_fix: Confirm the connected route and then correct the host gateway to 10.70.0.1.

symptom: A server is reachable from its LAN but replies to remote clients fail.
show_outputs:
Server: IP 172.16.5.50 Mask 255.255.255.0 Gateway 172.16.6.1
R2#show ip interface brief
G0/0 172.16.5.1 up up
expected_fault: Server default gateway is outside its local subnet.
expected_fix: Change server gateway to 172.16.5.1, then verify remote ping.

symptom: New PCs receive no IPv4 address.
topology_note: R1 provides DHCP for 192.168.10.0/24.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip dhcp pool
Pool LAN10
Network 192.168.10.0 /24
Default router 192.168.10.1
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/0 192.168.20.1 up up
expected_fault: DHCP pool serves 192.168.10.0/24 but R1 has no interface in that subnet; clients on G0/0 are on 192.168.20.0/24.
expected_fix: Align the DHCP pool/network with the client subnet or configure the intended LAN interface.

symptom: Clients receive 169.254.x.x addresses.
topology_note: R1 G0/0 is the DHCP server for VLAN 20.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip dhcp pool
Pool VLAN20
Network 192.168.20.0 /24
Default router 192.168.20.1
R1#show ip dhcp binding
Bindings: none
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/0 192.168.20.1 administratively down down
expected_fault: The router LAN interface is shutdown, so DHCP requests cannot reach the service.
expected_fix: Bring the intended interface up after human review and verify DHCP binding.

symptom: Some clients get addresses but cannot reach the gateway.
topology_note: DHCP serves VLAN 30 clients.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip dhcp pool
Pool VLAN30
Network 192.168.30.0 /24
Default router 192.168.30.254
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/1 192.168.30.1 up up
expected_fault: DHCP advertises gateway 192.168.30.254 while R1 interface is 192.168.30.1.
expected_fix: Change the DHCP default-router to the actual gateway 192.168.30.1.

symptom: DHCP pool is exhausted and new users cannot obtain addresses.
topology_note: A /29 lab network supports six usable client addresses.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip dhcp pool
Pool LAB
Network 10.0.0.0 /29
Total addresses 6
Leased addresses 6
R1#show ip dhcp binding
10.0.0.1  ...
10.0.0.2  ...
10.0.0.3  ...
10.0.0.4  ...
10.0.0.5  ...
10.0.0.6  ...
expected_fault: The DHCP pool has no free leases.
expected_fix: Review stale leases/reservations and expand the pool only if the topology permits.

symptom: Users can ping 8.8.8.8 but cannot open example.com.
topology_note: Clients use R1 as DNS forwarder and have internet connectivity.
show_outputs:
PC-A: IP 192.168.40.10 Mask 255.255.255.0 Gateway 192.168.40.1 DNS 192.168.40.1
R1#show running-config | include ip name-server
(no output)
expected_fault: No DNS server is configured on R1 even though clients are pointed to it.
expected_fix: Configure a reachable DNS server or point clients to the approved DNS server.

symptom: Only DNS name resolution fails; direct IP access to the web server works.
topology_note: Client DNS should be 192.168.50.53.
show_outputs:
PC-A: IP 192.168.50.10 Gateway 192.168.50.1 DNS 192.168.60.53
Server: DNS 192.168.50.53 up
R1#show ip route 192.168.50.0
C 192.168.50.0/24 is directly connected
expected_fault: Client DNS points to 192.168.60.53, while the reachable DNS server is 192.168.50.53.
expected_fix: Change the client DNS server to the approved reachable DNS server and test resolution.

symptom: Clients receive intermittent name-resolution failures.
topology_note: DNS server is on VLAN 60; ACL should allow UDP/TCP 53 from clients.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists
Extended IP access list CLIENT-FILTER
10 deny udp 192.168.60.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.60.53 eq domain
20 permit ip any any
R1#show ip interface g0/0
Internet address is 192.168.60.1/24
expected_fault: ACL explicitly denies DNS traffic from the client subnet to the DNS server.
expected_fix: Have a human review the security policy, then replace the incorrect deny with an approved DNS permit rule.

symptom: A lab hostname resolves to an old server address.
topology_note: Internal DNS server should return 10.10.10.20 for app.lab.local.
show_outputs:
PC-A> nslookup app.lab.local
Name: app.lab.local
Address: 10.10.10.99
DNS#show running-config | include app.lab.local
ip host app.lab.local 10.10.10.99
expected_fault: The static DNS/host entry maps app.lab.local to the wrong address.
expected_fix: Correct the approved host/DNS record to 10.10.10.20 and verify resolution.

symptom: LAN A can reach router but not LAN B.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip route
C 192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, G0/0
10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, G0/1
R2#show ip route
C 192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected, G0/0
expected_fault: R1 has no route toward 192.168.20.0/24.
expected_fix: Add the appropriate static/dynamic route after confirming the intended topology.

symptom: Remote branch network is unreachable from headquarters.
topology_note: R1 HQ and R2 branch are connected by 10.0.0.0/30.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip route 172.16.30.0
% Network not in table
R2#show ip route
C 172.16.30.0/24 is directly connected, G0/0
expected_fault: HQ R1 lacks a route to the branch network 172.16.30.0/24.
expected_fix: Configure the intended route via the R2 next hop or restore the routing protocol advertisement.

symptom: Traffic reaches the remote router but return traffic is lost.
topology_note: Two routers connect 10.1.1.0/30; R1 LAN is 192.168.1.0/24 and R2 LAN is 192.168.2.0/24.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip route 192.168.2.0
S 192.168.2.0/24 [1/0] via 10.1.1.2
R2#show ip route 192.168.1.0
% Network not in table
expected_fault: R2 lacks the return route to R1 LAN 192.168.1.0/24.
expected_fix: Add/restore the return route on R2 after human review.

symptom: A newly added network is not advertised to OSPF neighbors.
topology_note: R1 has LAN 192.168.50.0/24 and runs OSPF process 1.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip protocols
Routing Protocol is "ospf 1"
Networks: 10.0.0.0/30
R1#show ip route 192.168.50.0
C 192.168.50.0/24 is directly connected
expected_fault: The new LAN is connected but not included in OSPF network statements, so neighbors do not learn it.
expected_fix: Advertise the intended LAN in OSPF and verify with show ip ospf neighbor/route.

symptom: Users can reach the internet but cannot reach the internal web server.
topology_note: ACL should permit HTTPS to 10.20.20.10 from 10.20.10.0/24.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists
Extended IP access list WEB-FILTER
10 deny tcp 10.20.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.20.20.10 eq 443
20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL explicitly denies HTTPS from the user subnet to the internal web server.
expected_fix: Human must review policy before changing the deny; then apply the approved permit/deny order.

symptom: Ping works but SSH to a router is blocked.
topology_note: Management subnet 192.168.99.0/24 should be allowed to SSH to R1.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists MGMT
10 permit icmp 192.168.99.0 0.0.0.255 any
20 deny tcp 192.168.99.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 22
30 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL denies TCP port 22 from the management subnet.
expected_fix: Review the management policy and change the rule only with human approval.

symptom: Guest clients can reach an internal database server unexpectedly.
topology_note: Guest VLAN 80 should be isolated from 10.0.50.0/24.
expected_fault: The first ACL rule permits guest-to-database traffic before the broader internal deny.
expected_fix: Escalate for human security review; reorder rules only after confirming intended guest isolation.

symptom: DNS works but HTTP access to a public test site is blocked.
topology_note: Outbound ACL should allow TCP 80/443 from 192.168.60.0/24.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists OUTBOUND
10 permit udp 192.168.60.0 0.0.0.255 any eq domain
20 deny tcp 192.168.60.0 0.0.0.255 any eq www
30 permit tcp 192.168.60.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 443
expected_fault: ACL denies outbound HTTP (TCP/80) for the client subnet.
expected_fix: Have the reviewer confirm policy, then permit HTTP if it is approved.

symptom: Inside hosts have no internet access; NAT translations are empty.
topology_note: R1 translates 192.168.10.0/24 to the WAN interface.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip nat translations
Pro Inside global Inside local Outside local Outside global
(no entries)
R1#show ip nat statistics
Inside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/0
Outside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/1
Hits: 0 Misses: 42
expected_fault: No translations are being created despite inside/outside interfaces; the NAT rule/policy is missing or mismatched.
expected_fix: Review and configure the intended NAT/PAT rule for the inside subnet.

symptom: Only some LAN hosts get internet access.
topology_note: LAN is 192.168.20.0/24; PAT should cover the whole subnet.
show_outputs:
R1#show running-config | include ip nat inside source
ip nat inside source list 10 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload
R1#show access-lists 10
10 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.127
expected_fault: NAT ACL covers only 192.168.20.0/25, leaving the upper half of the /24 untranslated.
expected_fix: Expand the NAT ACL to the intended subnet after verifying the address plan.

symptom: NAT translations exist but users cannot connect externally.
topology_note: R1 G0/1 is the WAN interface and should be the NAT outside interface.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip nat statistics
Inside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/0
Outside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/2
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/1 203.0.113.2 up up
G0/2 unassigned administratively down down
expected_fault: NAT outside is assigned to the wrong/down interface; the actual WAN is G0/1.
expected_fix: Correct NAT outside role on the actual WAN interface after human review.

symptom: Port-forwarded internal web server is unreachable from the outside.
topology_note: Public address 203.0.113.10 should forward TCP/80 to 192.168.30.10.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip nat translations
Pro Inside global 203.0.113.10:8080 Inside local 192.168.30.10:80
R1#show running-config | include ip nat inside source static
ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.30.10 80 203.0.113.10 8080
expected_fault: Port forwarding is configured on external port 8080, while the requirement is public TCP/80.
expected_next_command: show running-config | include ip nat inside source static
expected_fix: Confirm the published port, then correct the static PAT rule if TCP/80 is the approved requirement.

symptom: Clients associate to the SSID but cannot obtain an IP address.
topology_note: AP bridges GuestWiFi to VLAN 80; DHCP is provided by R1.
show_outputs:
AP#show wireless vlan
SSID GuestWiFi VLAN 80
SW1#show vlan brief
80 GUEST active
SW1#show interfaces trunk
Fa0/1 trunking
Vlans allowed on trunk 10,20,30
R1#show ip dhcp pool
Pool GUEST network 192.168.80.0 /24
expected_fault: VLAN 80 is missing from the AP uplink trunk, so guest DHCP broadcasts cannot reach R1.
expected_fix: Allow VLAN 80 on the AP trunk and verify DHCP bindings.

symptom: Wireless clients connect but cannot reach the internet.
topology_note: Guest SSID uses VLAN 90; guest subnet is 192.168.90.0/24.
show_outputs:
AP#show wireless vlan
SSID Guest VLAN 90
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/2 192.168.90.1 up up
R1#show ip nat statistics
Inside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/1
Outside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/2
NAT ACL 15
R1#show access-lists 15
10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
expected_fault: Guest subnet 192.168.90.0/24 is not included in the NAT ACL, so guest traffic is not translated.
expected_fix: After human policy review, include the guest subnet in the approved NAT policy if internet access is intended.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi can access an internal file server, violating isolation requirements.
topology_note: Guest VLAN 100 should have internet-only access; internal server is 10.100.10.20.
show_outputs:
AP#show wireless vlan
SSID Guest VLAN 100
R1#show access-lists GUEST-IN
10 permit ip 192.168.100.0 0.0.0.255 10.100.10.0 0.0.0.255
20 permit ip 192.168.100.0 0.0.0.255 any
expected_fault: Guest ACL explicitly permits access to the internal server subnet.
expected_fix: Human security review is mandatory; remove/reorder the internal permit only if isolation is confirmed.

symptom: Clients see the SSID but fail authentication.
topology_note: WPA2-PSK should use the lab password configured on the AP and client.
show_outputs:
AP#show running-config | include ssid|wpa|passphrase
ssid LabWiFi
 authentication open
 wpa-psk ascii 0 LabNet2026
Client profile: SSID LabWiFi, WPA2-PSK, key LabNet2025
expected_fault: Client PSK does not match the AP PSK.
expected_fix: Correct the client key to the approved AP key or change the AP only with authorization; then retest.
